We vote for candidates. We also vote for principles. No issue is more of a core principle on your ballot than our fundamental right to vote. With Trump's MAGA movement working to suppress the vote and using government agencies to raid voter registration groups, the importance of this election is clear.
Please, Team, RUSH $35 or more right now to fuel our work to register, inform, and turn out every voter possible for the midterms >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=071426_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Our democracy is on your ballot this year, Team , seriously.
This isn’t just a figure of speech or hyperbole. More than a third of state ballot measures that voters like you will face this year relate to our democracy. On top of that, voters nationwide are electing the officials who will run the 2028 elections with their votes in the midterms.
That’s why our work to inform, register, and turn out voters is more important than ever. Pitch in $35 or whatever you can to help fuel our work for voting rights today >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=071426_3&amount=35]

By Election Day, voters will make decisions on voting rights, election processes, redistricting, and many other key electoral issues, let alone control of Congress, state legislatures, governorships, and more.
We have our chance to directly fight back against the voter suppression and voter discrimination we're seeing play out in real time from the anti-voting elected officials in power right now.

body:
I’m not sending this message to millions of people.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=7732%2E582294%2EffLdaW)
I know my team and I email you a lot to share updates about our campaign.
But today’s message is a little bit different. Let me tell you why:
Right now I’m only reaching out to _a smaller group of people like you_ – **people who have yet to make their first-ever donation to our campaign.**
I’m specifically emailing folks like you to ask for a big favor. With the GOP outspending us, I’m counting on your help in a major way.
**[Will you make your very first $5 donation to help us close the gap? We must raise $200,000 in order to keep pace with the massive flood of GOP spending coming into our state if we want a shot at flipping the Senate.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260714_3.w3bM0Q&refcode=em20260714-3&t=2&akid=7732%2E582294%2EffLdaW)**

Before I sat down to write this email, my team made sure I knew this about you:
According to our records, you have an opportunity to make TODAY the very first day you contribute to our campaign. Every donation – even a couple bucks – makes a difference in our fight to keep New Hampshire’s Senate seat, and **I’m relying on a few more first-time donors to step up.**
None of this is possible without you. **[So I’m asking you to consider making your first-ever $5 donation today. Every dollar we raise will help us close the gap and prove to the GOP that New Hampshire is not for sale.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260714_3.w3bM0Q&refcode=em20260714-3&t=22&akid=7732%2E582294%2EffLdaW)**
Thank you,
Chris Pappas

Should members of Congress be allowed to buy and sell individual stocks while making decisions that can move markets?
I don't think so.
While most Americans don't get access to private briefings, inside information, or advance knowledge of government actions, members of Congress do.
It’s no wonder so many people have lost faith in Washington. They look at the headlines, see politicians outperforming the market, and wonder whether the system is rigged for the powerful.
That's why I introduced legislation to ban members of Congress and their spouses from trading individual stocks while serving in office — because elected officials should be focused on serving the people who sent them to Washington, not managing investment portfolios.
But the reality is that reform only happens when enough people demand it. So today, I'm asking for your voice: Will you add your name if you agree that members of Congress should be banned from trading individual stocks while in office? [https://go.marieforcongress.com/a/ban-stock-trading]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://go.marieforcongress.com/a/ban-stock-trading]
Washington works best when the people have confidence that their representatives are acting in the public interest.
Let's take one step toward restoring that trust.
Thank you for speaking up.
— Marie

body:

---
| | | **[Thank You, E. Jean Carroll](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tddd27746-b5ec-43cd-8197-9709eedbdba3/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** [](https://default.salsalabs.org/T2fc27e74-bdcf-4d1e-ad35-7bf58c608c52/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) _**Breaking: Trump has finally [paid Carroll the $5+ million](https://default.salsalabs.org/T4c22ed63-4f31-4550-a83b-d2c99ed4d59b/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9). She persisted, and showed what real courage is like**_ She persisted, she won, and now **[Donald Trump has finally paid up](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tc1c81825-736a-4cc3-81fb-651cd7e9ce24/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** : _'“More than three years after [a jury found](https://default.salsalabs.org/T5ecd54da-077e-42aa-88d0-751da188286d/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) that President Donald Trump sexually abused and defamed E. Jean Carroll, she has received the $5.6 million awarded to her by jurors, court records show._ _Carroll had in 2019 accused Trump of sexually assaulting her in the mid-1990s. After he denied Carroll’s accusations and publicly assailed her, she filed two civil lawsuits. The first case went to trial in 2023 and ended with jurors awarding Carroll [$5 million](https://default.salsalabs.org/Te059e3a6-46d0-4a1f-ab07-a2de989efd51/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) in damages.”_ **[Sign your name: Thank you, E. Jean Carroll](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tafec48ee-8ede-4632-9d61-3603f268085f/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**

Thank you for your courage. Thank you for speaking out about what Donald Trump did.” Thank you for being a voice for justice.

**We stand with you. And we thank you. And we salute you.**

Trump is going to tell you Georgia's Senate seats were stolen and he is going to use this as a basis to try to cancel the midterms.
Here are the facts:
He has already floated canceling the midterms twice this year. In January he told Reuters, talking about the midterms and the seats Republicans could lose, "we shouldn't even have an election." He said something similar to a room full of House Republicans.￼
The White House said he was joking. When a reporter asked whether the President finds canceling elections funny, the press secretary asked him if he had been in the room.
He can't cancel them. No president can. The dates are set by statute and the elections are run by thousands of local officials in every state. Even the Republican former recorder of Maricopa County says the idea misunderstands how elections actually work.
Here's what he's doing instead: sowing distrust in elections so much that they can try to call off the elections.
Georgia Public Broadcasting went and counted. In the 1,387 precincts Trump won in November 2020, about 310,000 fewer people voted in the January runoffs. Ossoff won by 55,000. Warnock by 94,000. The dropoff in Trump's own precincts was more than double both margins combined.
The Atlanta Journal-Constitution went through the voting records and found 752,000 Georgians who cast a ballot in November and never came back in January. More than half were white. Many were rural. The steepest drops came in Marjorie Taylor Greene's district and Buddy Carter's.￼
Their poll found that more than three quarters of Georgia Republicans believed there had been widespread fraud. Four percent of Democrats did.
They found one of the men who stayed home. Craig Roland, 61, of Rome, Georgia. He told them he didn't believe his vote would count. "What good would it have done to vote?" He said he doesn't know if he'll ever vote again.
He didn't lose those seats to fraud. He talked his own voters out of voting, and Craig Roland is still not voting.￼
Here is what he did about it.
January 5, 9:03 in the morning. Kurt Olsen, who has spent years denying the 2020 election and now works in the White House, formally refers Fulton County to the Justice Department.
January 5, 8:36 that night. The same day. DOJ files to dismiss the civil lawsuit it had been using to try to obtain Fulton County's ballots.
January 28. FBI agents carry nearly 700 boxes out of the Fulton County elections warehouse. The original ballots. The tabulator tapes.￼
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bea81f96-f572-479b-b6f7-89265676aec5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The ballot images. Georgia's 2020 voter rolls. Legal experts told CNN the case moved unusually fast for its kind.
That timeline is not mine. It is the Justice Department's own, filed in court after a federal judge ordered them to produce it. Fulton County told the judge what they believe it was: a pretext to get records this administration could not secure through the civil process.￼
The chairman of the county commission said he was never told where the ballots went, and that he can no longer assure anyone they are secure.
The Director of National Intelligence, Tulsi Gabbard, was at the warehouse in person. At a county ballot depot in Union City, Georgia.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/218a3a71-bf73-4e22-afdd-03bb017bdf70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
His own Justice Department, in his first term, found no evidence of fraud that could have changed 2020.
On Thursday he is expected to announce newly declassified intelligence reports that, in MS NOW's careful wording, the White House says reveal foreign plans to interfere in the 2020 election. Read that phrasing again. Nobody is reporting that the documents show it. They are reporting that the White House says they do.
The Director of National Intelligence is the person who declassifies intelligence.￼
He told the New York Times that he always respects the results of elections, and then that the elections in this country are rigged. The election that has not happened yet is in November. By then the agency that certifies America's voting machines will still have zero members and still be unable to act. The Justice Department will still be holding Georgia's ballots.
He is not investigating the last election. He is building the case against the next one.￼
Georgia is not the exception. It's the model.
His DOJ is suing two dozen states for their voter rolls. Courts have repeatedly ruled these demands illegal.
It sent monitors into six states. Five have Democratic governors. Detroit's clerk says the monitors DOJ cited in its own letter were never there.
It sent letters to all fifty states threatening election officials with criminal prosecution.
One state's ballots. Twenty-four states' voter rolls. Fifty states' officials. The machines themselves.
And last week he fired both Democratic commissioners of the Election Assistance Commission by emai
The Republican had already quit. The agency that certifies America's voting machines has zero members and cannot act.
Raphael Warnock, one of the two senators Trump is about to call illegitimate, already told you what it's for: he is rigging the rules ahead of the midterms.
And the logic doesn't make sense:
Warnock has won 2 primaries, 2 generals, and 2 run offs.
Ossoff had to win a primary, a general, and a runoff.
Every piece of that was in place before a single vote is cast in November.
Thursday isn't about 2020. It's about 2026.￼

clean_body: Peter, I'm going to make a prediction... When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock. And the political establishment is going to spend weeks trying to explain what hit them. But that only happens if Republicans like you are on record before the Midterms. That is how consequential this moment is. But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either. I made you a prediction at the beginning of this email. I stand by every word of it. But that prediction is built on one assumption -- that Republicans like you are engaged and ready to fight. That is where your assessment comes in. The Department of War is getting a Drone Czar, and it's time to secure American Drone Dominance with smart, America First partnerships.
LOOMER UNLEASHED is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..scvcag2m50uwGpfosNWZg21pR5RaNXJTHmS3CAgMnMI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=207112158)
In a decisive move to supercharge America's unmanned systems capabilities, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has [established ](https://substack.com/redirect/ac9e25dd-581c-4c05-be7b-b3cf46613e17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)a new Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager for Unmanned Systems (DRPM-UxS), widely dubbed the "Drone Czar." This newly established and high-level office within the Pentagon will serve as the single joint integrator for nearly all unmanned and autonomous programs across the Department of War, overseeing tens of billions of dollars in investments spanning air, land, and sea. Reporting directly to the Deputy Secretary of War, the drone czar will cut through bureaucratic red tape, accelerate procurement, and ensure the U.S. military maintains its edge in the drone warfare revolution that's reshaping battlefields worldwide.
This isn't just another layer of bureaucracy, but rather a strategic necessity in the world of evolving warfare. Adversaries like China and Russia are flooding the skies with cheap, lethal drones. Ukraine's real-world combat experience has proven the game-changing power of mass-produced, innovative unmanned systems. By centralizing authority under a Drone Czar, the Department of War is signaling that drone dominance is now a top priority for American defense. From swarming tactics to autonomous ground vehicles and maritime drones, this office will drive rapid innovation, integration, and manufacturing at record speed.
Tied directly into this push is the recently [highlighted ](https://substack.com/redirect/c5f5388a-3389-4c2f-936e-62f411fb6e40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)drone manufacturing collaboration with Ukraine. While discussions and drafts have been advancing, Ukrainian firms are showcasing battle-tested technology and interest in U.S. partnerships for production on American soil. These efforts align with broader "[Drone Deal](https://substack.com/redirect/9f7fdccf-f3a0-4121-92f0-6ae271ab7c72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" initiatives where Ukraine has inked agreements with multiple partners to share expertise, enable joint production, and transfer knowledge from the front lines.
For American Drone Dominance to come to fruition, it is necessary for Ukrainian companies to partner with an American firm. The drone deal with Ukraine is not yet signed, and it has come to my attention that no such partnership mandate exists. Of the nine countries that have signed drone deals with Ukraine, the majority required such a partnership.
While there is no question that a US deal for Ukrainian drones should be executed, it is imperative that a vetted, trusted US business builds out the sector rather than a fly-by-night foreign company. We have no visibility into their supply chain, ownership, or security. A mandated partnership with American companies is the only way to ensure that America First values are satisfied with a Ukrainian drone deal.
This approach protects critical technology, secures supply chains against foreign influence or vulnerabilities, and keeps high-value manufacturing jobs and intellectual property here in the United States. Ukrainian innovation, which is honed in brutal combat, is invaluable, but it must be channeled through American companies that prioritize U.S. national security, comply with strict export controls, and align with our strategic goals. No unchecked foreign entities should gain unfettered access to our defense industrial base.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..scvcag2m50uwGpfosNWZg21pR5RaNXJTHmS3CAgMnMI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=207112158)
The new Drone Czar has a massive mandate ahead: integrating these partnerships responsibly while scaling domestic production. Imagine American factories churning out next-gen drones informed by Ukrainian lessons, backed by U.S. engineering, funding, and oversight. This could close capability gaps, deter adversaries, and position the U.S. as the undisputed leader in autonomous warfare for decades to come.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/f600c560-2391-443c-94ba-71be8a2cd7b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
There is no denying that true dominance requires control over design, production, maintenance, and oversight, including transparency in every link of the chain. With the Drone Czar in place, there's an opportunity at the Pentagon to set the right precedents now: America leads, American firms build, and our allies contribute under our framework.
This is bigger than one deal or one office. It's about reclaiming the innovation edge, revitalizing our defense industrial base, and ensuring that every dollar spent on drones strengthens U.S. security first. The battlefield of tomorrow is already here, and it's playing out before our eyes in wars from Russia, Ukraine, Gaza, and Iran, where swarms of low-cost drones are overwhelming expensive traditional defense systems.
The United States must respond to this evolving warfare with urgency, discipline, and an unapologetic focus on American strength and American dominance in manufacturing on US soil.
The establishment of a Drone Czar is a strong first step. Now, as the Ukraine manufacturing partnership moves forward, Secretary Hegseth has an opportunity to do this the right way: vetted U.S. partners, full visibility, and America First outcomes and American dominance.
The time is now, and our military, our workers, and our future depend on it.

Turns out there's a science to why faces stick, but names slip away, plus a [few tricks to fix](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O6yAUBOCnwR0WYGI7BcVt3OW2W1oHOA5s-LGADcrbr7LFvsB2U3wajebjtt_AB5_u_yGiakfeE_YasDUsuy-QOhQN5pGTQwjNGShYz10wMVO2UH7ZLfjw2uVg1YEocBpQ8WWVnDM-8cEpbbXgh7F8PbSZrnzSC0N-vcwz6hXsPHj1bmMLv3DGVnkd9SGlNciXWctJ8JVIhta3XMbP7FNzeIRXfmIZTY5DUK61s5LpHxEbEVvvfYTS8hEhBZ-w1jcjYqvZeAi_gdaHD6ESsbncacu0YMSosVCgJ5aaU6UJIlJIlnYH7W1spt1hoq_8RQ2kRsQ2FGXP7kPwdV6IZPcIPvwsa3-686nEdwAAAP__lE2MUQ) it in today's _Wisdom Wednesday_. ## Trump Notifies Congress of Resumed Iran War
President Trump notified Congress that the United States has [resumed war against Iran](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD0O3CAUhE-DOyzA-GcLim3cbaRUKa1n_LBfgsECdtHePnKukG6kkUbzfb9eywvIU9h_wImmuLgErNljKZgWShAqpBXsnxgOBF8OCwnztSihBi5GLvtlA_LfRTebcYgKuwaNHCctpZCdbA6jANZhnR6i36Qb9CaslM6NuluVBZRrQ-ZeE6PspRCTfrSr03qzKMdh1Z2SE9MCNyoxtb8jhXKg89_4wdTaeDbeHKVcmXVPpmam5lpre-Zwd0zNGPg7MzXfUEzNV_RUyN6xpPd58RALOcLMbQx7wpx5dDxg5RUShx0o5MJvDUzNkPjzqcafvd2bZLarkveUh5FpsZ9A_t-d8l8OP0b9DQAA___HfYcN), invoking the War Powers Act and restarting a 60-day clock for congressional approval after a ceasefire collapsed over attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. forces have struck Iranian missile sites, air defenses, and naval assets for three straight nights. On Tuesday, Trump also [scrapped a proposed 20% toll](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1u7CAQxfGnwZ1XgPFXQXEbd3vblNbYDMskGCyY7GrfPnJeIfVf-knnfNzXO1Ck9PgPB1r2eU34qhGZsaxUIL2gbLB_5RQQIocdCtZz1VIPrRxb1a8OKL5X0zjrETV2DVo1TkYpqTrVBLvv0oAeAb3cPE5z3znjcNiGyUkPcmjIXpocVa-knMx827wxbkc1DpvptJqEkeiIc7l9Zkoc0Md3fmK57floog3MZxXdP6EXoRcOGCjGqwm9hHzgNUjoBdxBiSoXYMpJ6KWfh7FXc8vl-zjbuhc4a3t14pZzjEIvTbHufFGMVIdRGPk4gH7phv_01dPqnwAAAP__xPl-0g) on cargo transiting the strait, opting instead for trade and investment deals with Gulf states, while pressing ahead with a blockade targeting only Iranian ships. Oil climbed to a one-month high on the news. Trump hosted Iraq's prime minister at the White House Tuesday, who said after that all U.S. forces would [leave Iraq](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2O5CAUBODT4IwWYPzTAcEmZL3phtYzPNpvBxsP0G15Tj_yXGHikj5V1b_H9ACKtD3_woqmhjRteJSItWKeKMN2QJ7BfaRtQYh1cZCx7JMSqudi4LKbPFA8J914ExAVtg0aOYxaSiFb2SxG97OYgw5eOzXeewzYdijHLnRj2_fgGjKXJgbZSSFGfb_NQWvvUA79rFslR6YFeqop3_4n2uqCIZ7pjfnm0tpEs9S6F9b-YcoyZbdzT6VeEVP2gpmyYmDKSs2UfRV-7WPKQoz8VXhI2WHhNfGD6uIzHDzktHLK8MnnkxfcK28Fh8i_gDwxZZts_H5QjFT6gWnxXIHiT5f6qwPfRn0HAAD__1Qog0Q) by Sept. 30, part of a pivot from military ties to energy and trade.
## 130 Million Americans Under Heat Wave Alerts
A massive heat wave stretching from Los Angeles to Boston is putting more than [130 million Americans under heat alerts](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1urDAQhZ_GdCCPPYvZwsVt6Pa2KdFghsWJ-ZE9WrJvH5FXSHekI52j7_t4DA-KKW7P_7Syl3kfNj5LYhHOQ8y0nZRHCl_7tjAlWQJlLsdgtGlr7Wq4DRPF9B6wmvzMbNhW7MF1CKDBQrV4CmDtyEgdIN47N7a245YRQ2AHd6iiv9a0gxto3eG9GWfEKTC4dkRroFOoeYqy5-Zzj5ssPKf3_uLchH2tkl9EjqLsP2V6ZfrzPJswlovi6pXpr6hMv9JR6iIkXGr-lswr1wuT1JniNlNKyvRV9tNxxpRiaZ1C_Vwppt8b-ZOblzc_AQAA__96UHj4) this week, with temperatures running 20 to 30 degrees above normal across the northern Plains and the Northeast. Records are already falling. More heat is coming. It will peak in the Northeast on Wednesday, with heat indices near 105 in Washington and 100 in New York City. ## Floods Swamp Hill Country
Up to 12 inches of rain had swamped Uvalde County by Tuesday morning, and forecasters warn hard-hit areas west of San Antonio could see [another 10 to 20 inches](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO6yAURVeDO1u8B5hQUPzGXX47pYXNc0AiYGEmTnY_SqRZwdRXOlfnfF3nq4sp5tt_dyfbnluZM51HotaoziGmtJbv3OprS6X4mG_H7mJeZuQ49lz3oGbvYnrNsvN24d5ARxb0RQIIMWIX7OaAxoWUEiMBOO9BXYzRTghhQBvVRfuGcQ0KgKMwgyAy4yoQuZQLbsgkJx9bqUML1Ojpji29yoPqsJZ7l2xobT-Y-MdwYjid5zmsoZb8XhlObx2Gk6strokYTh9C_-vTI-9jXgMdPaKQUmkY9rB31fr9jCnFY9RM8tvdxfT5a3-r9LD4EwAA___kVHsX). Crews in Medina County made at least [four water rescues](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbuu4yAQQL_G7ibCAzGhcLGNu7vtlhaPsUEhYAGJb_5-5az2C259NDPnaP58LV86xJC23_pBU_te85LoqJFao7L4EKPNz9TKe405u5C2uuuQzIIMR2AShuvidIjvRfRuMsypoadpkDcxDJyP2PuJcXkb11HejCOnjHEaOWeOK-6MNcr2YTqXMTlch4EhVxdOpEbLEZkQBlfsBCMXWi6X5qnRt65rfOcXlYvNjz5OvrW9dvxXh3OH83Eclzulej1ph7MuLdhIHc5nWIdzzFbHDuet0AbamNwa_K-DNerqgR5UNkr2DYXqnlMl-NyFpFvISUfYnro4MFHbu9fHHdxeoR5hbYduVM4x-yTwFIPNe6NSwYfN_4Mv8qfR6YKSg0Q-ClQM2M2NIJxRYJRUsDphmNBScmn7Mrn9CDGGOspOsO2hQ_zkt5897TXh3wAAAP__xIKvFA) after 3 to 9 inches of rain fell overnight. Gov. Greg Abbott [declared a disaster in 59 counties](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb_GdI7swUAoXGxD97bdEg14DJYGO7L9SPL3KyLt_sDrphhdnXP-fM1fGDjE7TceZOvLpznSszDVSnneA_OavmPNb88puRC38sAQlxkU9FINUnezw8Dv2TTOLsqNuiGrh7vRum17aHbbdQOBcqjvvVfeoIehxX5xSvXe0b1rgr3G1KA7rRW0460lGvu1BVDGLOBBGEUu1JRvdadKLyye3-mkfFvT0bDda30U0f4SMAmYCkaMG3HicNL1IWC6lARM6bu6lPJ1_uc3AqbPpnS0MmYq0oWCpVKW3Sg_9oGKxCM4WeikTLLUlI8iMTrpGcsu_8VpsnWPZ2AOpR-EUduBgT-U9WdtTwt_AwAA___ucpAj) and kept the state's emergency operations center running around the clock. Swiftwater rescue teams and National Guard Black Hawk helicopters were staged across the state. More rounds of heavy rain are forecast [into Wednesday and Thursday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL_GZB7ZjYEjILiEbC-9EPXg9ri1Hntk9w7L35_YX7iwVFK9qvr7sX0gJ86PP_ikRb5D2TIdLZEI1S1ySnv5ylLPkErxnB_thZzvGxgYtZm0HTaPnM7NdX65Gz_bjhY7_XLW9v0IXVzIj7s14-zQEA0hDHbw43yf0dlhtLPreLnCzGQHaw30860nmse9BzDO3SGAcoY8S6k3iST0jS2ks7yp3vby7NISRV5N9b8VrArW4zhunw3lMi9JKJGqgvWiKFjNpGC1TsH6M0lXbp96L1k4f1HTkfB96oqcdcSmA6ZEWV-0zI8omtqLdsaUTn1QE12Cbpg1ZimZi4K1q4t_HZwSt3FSzjyeyOmnqfzfv-8F_gUAAP__PzaQiQ), with the highest flood threat along the U.S. 90 corridor west of San Antonio and north into the Hill Country.
## ICE Pauses Most Vehicle Stops
ICE has ordered agents to [suspend most vehicle stops](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGyqyAQhp8GOxxYiMaC4jZ0ue0tHZRFd4LgCDcmb3_GvMLZdmf3-_7_32N8OIqUlr9uQ1PfIY8JzxKxVjzGlWKc8_9Uj0-IOXtKS9kdpWkEAR0XPZe30TuKn1E33kzCD7JBI_u7llKpDprVKKdxUNp5hTev-2umrpchTMrfg5INmeuZ6OVNSgFqaBXi0M0KQGg9QQCmBXqq-WjrihXfroT4yS882jlvTTRrrXth6g8Dy8Ce59k-i6vXkoG90jCwMc8uMrAXioEVPQMrNQN74J6PWjjNyFcXK6WFl7whf-FKc0Reat4Lp8RP90SeA_8a8M1RQl7WnK-TC9Ecxu8nxUil65kWy-YofhXr74p9GfgJAAD__x3fjXA) nationwide after officers fatally shot two men during stops in Texas and Maine over the past week. Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 52-year-old Mexican illegal immigrant living in Houston, was killed on July 7 when agents stopped his van while pursuing a different man. The Department of Homeland Security said he tried to ram an officer; [his family disputes that account](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SgyAUhZ8GOzJw_SEWFNvQZdstHYSr3lkUB4iJb79jXmHbc2bOz_fzGB6WAm3zt11Rl_cUhw1fOWApmIaFQnDxuZV0TiFGT9ucd0vbOICAjgvFZTt4S-EcmsrrUfheVqilujdS1nUH1aJ7VKJWapLoverd6GQnJ5Bji_beTtZVpK8woWQrpYC6v9WIfedqANE0I0zAGoGeSky3smDBt81TOOOB6ebiWgW9lLJnVn8xMAzM70H2MhiY6wkDM8bkMTEwVw8DIxQDIxsGhhzyEnnBdY_JJgonzyXu3MXNP12hbeYHLuQCfvTMc3wmh5lnezIwVdJ-f1EIlDvFGjGvlsJnVPkfykPDXwAAAP__I_SJHA). The pause is temporary while agents [get more training](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE9jMiO7wTAEDjYhm003RMa0oSVjI9w7zNz-i7nCz0oqqZ5e_XtOT0eR0vrX7Wj5HfKU8CoRmfGcNorR5_-Jz0-IOS-U1nI4SvMECjqpeqnNtDiKn6mtFjurZdAVWt0_Wq2bpoNqs30w3jxwgDa4AMZ1Te-8Cdi5sBjjVUX2HlO9NloraIa6QRw63wCotp0hgGgVLsT5rHlDxrcrIX7yC8_a572KdmM-imj-CBgFjNd11X4ut8XdCxjvKGAkj9KtmLjIzUWWL9zIR5SF81GkC4ynLFvOfFvK3VFC-aUJGKvTLsdFMVLpetGqdXcUv3j-3WkvCz8BAAD__2bUg-E) on vehicle-stop tactics, and it won't apply to operations targeting serious criminal suspects. Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, said she urged Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to [halt non-urgent stops](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ8GOiN77QApXFxDl2uvRI69DistGNlOCG9_4n-Fv5tiNJrv-_eYH46Yttdft6Kt35jmDY_CWCvmeSFmn95bzWfklAJtr7I72p4zSOiFHIS6zcERn7Npg33KcFctWjWMRimte2gXOwKgc3I0CEoh4mD8qEI_hAhSooaW7DUmB3VTSoK-dxrx3nsNII15QoTGSAxUU-7qghW_rkQ-0wdz59Pasl1q3Uuj_zQwNTAdx9HF9DUXxlVoYLpiAxN5FLSuGMhV5FN4dAXFmkoVH1zIM4pS015ExIDZsSjpnT0WUdxZ2mzDfhAzlX5ojHytjvjnQP2dto-F_wEAAP__9OGEig). Rep. Christian Menefee, D-Houston, said the pause doesn't go far enough: "_A temporary training won't solve a deeply ingrained problem._ "
## $469M Mesquite Ammo Plant Under Scrutiny
A $469 million Army ammunition plant in Mesquite, east of Dallas, has produced no usable [155mm artillery projectile parts](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAYhJ9GOwz8oq4FxTV2e-2VBuRHSX7BALuub3_xXuG6SSYzk_l-nvNTe_Jh_dY7qvJxcQ54ZsJSMM2bJ1riK5R0OYrR-rDmQ_tgZuDQMz4w0c1We7pmWVtluB1FjUoMDylE2_ZQb2rphQTdgXXgRngY44BLI6TVDo0Yde3VXcYH0QnBoR2bFnHslxaAS2nAQSU5Wl9iasqGBT86O7riG1OzxL0mtZVy5Kr9qmCqYDrPs1lMvl_cfgXTLSuYLDoMGdmpy7LZuDLRdfvOdCqeCNPFDtKhsCNF-1qKj4GtUdOdrJOyx-mJfO6HSvJ1157-xsv_kL0V_AYAAP__HUCCyw) in the roughly two years since it opened, a Pentagon watchdog found. The Defense Department inspector general's report, released Monday, said the plant hadn't produced any metal parts that met contract specifications as of March. The Army aims to produce 100,000 rounds per month after sending more than 3 million shells to Ukraine. It was producing [about 36,000 rounds](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOozAQBOCnMR3IXhtIChfX0OXaK5HB69jSgpG9F8Lbn3L69b_A385Io0_z5zE_XKK0P3-7DS2_Q553PCshM5Y5JqI1_925XIFy9ml_1sOlfZlBwtDKsVX97F2iazaNt4v0d9WgVePNKKX1AE20zgAE34-LUqCdN-ttQaO9wluvgkdokv2MyVH1SknQ904j3odVA0hjFgggjESfOJeOIzK-XQ105ReWbs1bQzYyH1XoXwImAdN5nl3lkg6sn17AtBS3rxGrgMmV7RIwfevNV9a6wokIy9XWiERtjblwcEQtAAwgR9lF3qgp1h9nIkp1GIWRz80l-s_gn533svAvAAD__4q2gyM) per month as of March. Inspectors traced the failure to a plan to [adapt older equipment for newer shells](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLuupiAUhZ8GOwxsEY4FxTR0Z9opDcpWSbgYwOPv20-cV5huFSvr8v35nr-tDz7tv21E3T5bnhPeNWBrWObDh7DmK7XybCFn59NeT-vTMgMDSZmifJyd9eGZRef0wtzEO9RcfQnOh0FCd-htBSm5XawdhVsmsTAnFVNcqi_L5DR1Xr9hTPGRcwbD1A-Ik1wHACbEAhsQwdD5lkvfDmz4sXULT_7B0q85dkEfrZ2VDL8IGALmvu_e4Yap4vvk9RAwryRgnnwVGn3wzZaHgHmbCRimCBguCJho07XZtV3Fp53eGSs9bDyx0KtSPo40RmpjzPQs2V1r8zkRMF3R7rx9CL5KRQTbo_Xh37r2f0x_NPwNAAD__368i2U), a risk the report says Army officials "accepted." With Mesquite idle, three plants in Pennsylvania and Canada are carrying the load. Operator General Dynamics said it and the Army have agreed on a path forward that includes additional company investment to finish the project.
